author: Lorenzo J. Reyna
title: Oregon Gets Good News on 4-Star WR Recruit Before Indiana Game - NewsBreak
text:
By Lorenzo J. Reyna ,
28 minutes ago
The Oregon Ducks look bound to attract a sellout crowd inside Autzen Stadium Saturday with Indiana in town.
This top 10 battle of Big Ten heavyweights now includes good news for the host Ducks. All involving a prized four-star wide receiver.
Which 4-Star WR is Visiting Oregon-Indiana? Oregon quarterback Dante MooreMatthew O'Haren-Imagn Images
Allen Trieu of 247Sports revealed Milan Parris will be taking in Eugene soon.
"Oregon will get a visit this week," the recruiting insider shared.
Parris reopened his recruiting process by backing off from his verbal commitment to Iowa State. He even made the decision following the Cyclones' upset loss to Cincinnati -- handing ISU its first loss of the season.
Oregon isn't the only power conference representative expected to host Parris.
"Miami was going to get Parris to visit during his bye week but he will now take an official for October 25th's game against Stanford," Trieu added.
Trieu includes Auburn will get Parris in its building -- for the famed annual Iron Bowl clash against Alabama on Nov. 29.
Oregon Target Brings Intrigue at WR Parris will be highly coveted as the college football version of a recruiting free agent aiming to sign elsewhere.
The Star of Walsh Jesuit High in Stow, Oh., landed 26 total offers before choosing the Big 12 powerhouse. Now he's considered "warm" on Oregon, Miami, Oklahoma and Auburn. It's not known if Parris aims to squeeze in a trip to Norman before the season ends.
Andrew Ivins of 247Sports compared his game to past Cyclones star Jayden Higgins, who's now with the Houston Texans.
"Imposing outside receiver with all the physical tools to bake into a touchdown machine on Saturdays and then potentially Sundays," was the first sentence Ivins wrote in his prospect evaluation.
Ivins adds how Parris "owns one of the best size-speed combinations in the class as he has gone 4.54 on the lasers in the 40-yard dash at close to 200 pounds."
That speed will fit nicely at "Duck Territory." Oregon has thrived with fast moving wideouts and has one now via Dakorien Moore.
